title: Nano Banana API Pricing: Cost Per Image in 2026
summary: Nano banana api pricing costs $0.0336 to $0.24 per image depending on tier and resolution. See which tier fits your usage and budget needs.
body_markdown:
## Hidden costs and limits that break budgets


Before you trust the headline price, know the four charges it leaves out, because they decide what a kept image costs: output resolution, input images, quota ceilings and refused or retried requests. Each is documented by Google except where marked below.


### Resolution changes the price per image


Metered per generated image, Nano Banana 2 still charges a rate that depends on output size.[Granata Labs](https://www.granatalabs.com/ai/image) lists 0.045 $ at 512px, 0.067 $ at 1K, 0.101 $ at 2K and 0.151 $ at 4K.


4K costs about 3.4 times the 512px rate, so a team that defaults to 4K for drafts pays for pixels it discards.


At 1,000 images, 1K costs $67 and 4K costs $151, so **upgrading to 4K more than doubles the cost** . That's a gap of $84. Generate at 512px or 1K while iterating and render at 2K or 4K only the image you intend to keep.


*(Chart sits here.)*


At 0.101 $, the 2K rate is 1.5 times the 1K rate, so 2K is the cheaper way to get a larger final file when 4K isn't needed.


Before generation even starts, every reference photo or edit source adds a charge, because Google bills input images as tokens.


An edit that sends three reference images costs more than a plain text prompt, and the extra is repeated on every retry. Budget the inputs per attempt, not per project.


### Rate limits and free-tier restrictions


A batch job that fits your budget can still stall on RPD.


Google sets quotas in requests per minute (RPM), tokens per minute (TPM) and requests per day (RPD), and applies them per project and tier, so check your tier's published limits before you size a run.


On the free tier, different data terms apply too: Google's documentation says unpaid-tier content may be used to improve its products. Client images should go through a paid tier. Paid tiers are also the route to higher quotas.


### Nano Banana API refused prompts and retry costs


When a safety filter refuses a prompt or an output, you still pay a retry's worth of time and tokens for inputs. Because a retry bills at the same resolution, a 4K retry costs 0.151 $ each time it repeats.


Don't expect refusals to be predictable: community reports, which aren't documentation, say they are inconsistent across near-identical prompts.


Treat claims that blocked requests are free as unverified until your own billing export confirms it. Log refusals as a separate line so the kept-image cost shows what they add.


That logging is where a second meter can creep in.


Activepieces has unlimited flows on every plan, including free, so a router, a retry counter, a spend log and an alert add no flow charge; credits meter AI usage, bring-your-own-key is available from the paid tiers up, and AI caps can be set per project and per person.


The free plan gives you 1,000 credits a month with unlimited flows, and MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run it in production.
